heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 can melt eSUN ABS+ at an effective volumetric flow rate of 18 mm³/s, unlocking a safe maximum print speed of 214 mm/s at standard layer heights. However, because the A1 is an open-frame bedslinger, successful printing requires an external enclosure or draft shield to prevent severe warping and delamination.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate + PVP glue stick (applied as an adhesion promoter and release agent)
slicerTweaks: Set Bed Temperature to 98°C for all layers and Nozzle Temperature to 250°C to maximize inter-layer adhesion without exceeding A1 bed limits.
Limit Part Cooling Fan to 0% base speed and a maximum of 15-20% only for overhangs shorter than 2 seconds to prevent premature thermal shrinkage.
Enable a 5mm outer brim with 0mm Brim-object gap to mechanically anchor sharp corners directly to the build plate.
Set Max Volumetric Speed cap to 18 mm³/s in the filament profile and enable Draft Shield mode to isolate the part from ambient cross-breezes.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe corner lifting and bed detachment
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: High thermal contraction coefficient combined with open-bed ambient drafts causing uneven cooling at the base.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Increase bed temperature to 98°C, apply a fresh coat of PVP glue stick, add an external tent enclosure or tall draft shield, and add a 6mm mouse-ear brim.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Inter-layer cracking (delamination) midway through tall prints
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Open-air convective cooling dropping the ambient temperature below the glass transition threshold, stalling layer-to-layer molecular diffusion.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Turn off part cooling completely (0%), reduce print speed to 150 mm/s to elevate ambient thermal radiation from the nozzle, and isolate the machine inside an enclosure.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Surface popping, roughness, and localized stringing
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption by the ABS+ filament boiling off inside the 250°C hotend melt zone.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament in an active filament dryer at 70°C for 6 to 8 hours before printing, and ensure direct feed from a sealed dry box.

faq.question: Can I print eSUN ABS+ safely on the Bambu Lab A1 without an enclosure?
faq.answer: Only for very small, low-profile parts under 30mm tall using a draft shield and brim. Medium to large parts will inevitably warp or crack without a passive enclosure or draft-free enclosure tent.

faq.question: Will the stock stainless steel nozzle on the A1 wear out with eSUN ABS+?
faq.answer: No, eSUN ABS+ does not contain abrasive additives like carbon fiber or glass fiber, making the stock stainless steel nozzle completely safe to use.

faq.question: Why is the bed temperature limited to 98°C instead of the recommended 100-105°C?
faq.answer: The Bambu Lab A1 has a hardware safety maximum bed temperature of 100°C; targeting 98°C ensures stable thermal regulation without tripping firmware protection limits.

faq.question: Is it safe to put the Bambu Lab A1 inside a full third-party enclosure?
faq.answer: Yes, but ensure the ambient chamber temperature does not exceed 45-50°C to prevent mainboard and stepper motor driver overheating, as the A1 electronics are not actively vented outside the chassis.
